source_text: εἰς ἀπόδειξιν τῆς Σολομῶντος ζωῆς τὴν κατάληξιν, καὶ ἅπερ αὐτῷ συνέβη παθεῖν, ἐπ' αὐτῷ γήρως οὐδῷ; {ΠΑΛΛ.} Πῶς ἔφης; {ΚΥΡ.} Ἦν μὲν γὰρ οὕτω λαμπρὸς καὶ ἀοίδιμος, ὡς ἀσύγκριτον ἤδη πως τὴν δόξαν ἑλεῖν, μετέθει γε μὴν εἰς τὸ ἀκαλλὲς, μᾶλλον δὲ καὶ κατέθορεν ἀγεννῶς, ἐς αὐτό που τὸ λοῖσθον τῆς εἰς Θεὸν ἀσεβείας. Ἔχει δὲ ὧδε τὰ ἐπ' αὐτῷ. Γέγραπται γὰρ ἐν τῇ τρίτῃ τῶν Βασιλειῶν· «Καὶ ἐμεγαλύνθη Σολομὼν ὑπὲρ πάντας τοὺς βασιλεῖς τῆς γῆς πλούτῳ καὶ φρονήσει. Καὶ πάντες οἱ βασιλεῖς τῆς γῆς ἐζήτουν τὸ πρόσωπον Σολομὼν, τοῦ ἀκοῦσαι τῆς φρονήσεως αὐτοῦ, ἧς ἔδωκε Κύριος ἐν τῇ καρδίᾳ αὐτοῦ.» Ἀλλὰ τὸν οὕτως εὐκλεᾶ καὶ ἀοίδιμον, καὶ σοφίας εἰς τοῦτο διεληλακότα λοιπὸν, ὡς ἐν ἀμετρήτῳ γενέσθαι θαύματι, καὶ παρά γε τοῖς ἄγαν διωρισμένοις, ἡδονὴ γυναίων ἐξεμόχλευσε πονηρῶν, καὶ οἱονείπως αὐτῆς ἐξελοῦσα τῆς θείας σκηνῆς τοῖς τῆς εἰδωλολατρείας ἐνῆκε βόθροις. Γέγραπται γὰρ ὡδὶ περὶ αὐτοῦ· «Καὶ ὁ βασιλεὺς Σολομὼν ἦν φιλογύναιος, καὶ ἔλαβε γυναῖκας ἀλλοτρίας, καὶ τὴν θυγατέρα Φαραώ· Μωαβίτιδας, καὶ Ἀμμονίτιδας, καὶ Ἰδουμαίας, Σύρας, Χετταίας, Ἀμοῤῥαίας, ἐκ τῶν ἐθνῶν, ὧν ἀπεῖπε Κύριος τοῖς υἱοῖς Ἰσραήλ· Οὐκ εἰσελεύσεσθε πρὸς αὐτοὺς, καὶ αὐτοὶ οὐκ εἰσελεύσονται πρὸς ὑμᾶς, ἵνα μὴ ἐκκλίνωσι τὰς καρδίας ὑμῶν ὀπίσω τῶν εἰδώλων αὐτῶν. Εἰς αὐτοὺς ἐκολλήθη Σολομὼν, τοῦ ἀγαπῆσαι. Καὶ ἦσαν αὐτῷ γυναῖκες ἄρχουσαι ἑπτακόσιαι, καὶ παλλακαὶ τριακόσιαι. Καὶ ἐγενήθη ἐν τῷ καιρῷ γήρως Σολομὼν, καὶ ἐξέκλιναν αἱ γυναῖκες αἱ ἀλλότριαι τὴν καρδίαν αὐτοῦ ὀπίσω θεῶν ἑτέρων. Καὶ οὐκ ἦν ἡ καρδία αὐτοῦ τελεία μετὰ Κυρίου Θεοῦ αὐτοῦ, καθὼς ἡ καρδία τοῦ Δαβὶδ τοῦ πατρὸς αὐτοῦ. Καὶ ἐπορεύθη Σολομὼν ὀπίσω τῆς Ἀστάρτης βδελύγματος Σιδωνίων, καὶ ὀπίσω τοῦ βασιλέως αὐτῶν εἰδώλου υἱῶν Ἀμμών· καὶ ἐποίησε Σολομὼν πονηρὸν ἐνώπιον Κυρίου, καὶ οὐκ ἐπορεύθη ὀπίσω Κυρίου, ὡς Δαβὶδ ὁ πατὴρ αὐτοῦ.» Ἆρ' οὐκ ἐποιμώζειν ἄξιον τῷ τοιάδε παθεῖν λεγομένῳ; Ὁ τὸν διαβόητον ἐκεῖνον ἐν τοῖς Ἱεροσολύμοις ἀναστήσας ναὸν, ὁ τὴν τῶν θείων θρόνων πάρεδρον αἰτήσας σοφίαν, ὁ ἐπὶ συνέσει τῇ ἀσυγκρίτῳ τεθαυμασμένος, καὶ μέχρις αὐτῶν τερμάτων τῆς ὑπ' οὐρανόν, ὁ καθάπερ ἑωσφόρος, πόλεσί τε καὶ χώραις ἐκφανὴς, αἰσχρῶν γυναικῶν ἡττώμενος, καὶ μυσαρωτάτης ἡδονῆς κατόπιν ἰὼν, εἰς τοῦτο μωρίας φωρᾶται πεσὼν, ὡς καὶ αὐτῆς ἀλογῆσαι παντελῶς τῆς εἰς Θεὸν εὐσεβείας. Σφαλερὸν οὖν ἄρα καὶ ἀναμφιλόγως ἐστὶ τὸ τοῖς ἀλλοφύλοις εἶναι κατὰ ταὐτόν. Πάνδεινον δὲ κομιδῇ καὶ τὸ ἡδονῆς ἡττᾶσθαι τῆς σαρκικῆς, καὶ ἀκάθαρτος ὁ τοιόσδε, καὶ τῷ πανάγνῳ Θεῷ κατεστυγημένος, καὶ οὐκ ἀρετῆς δίχα, πρὸς τὴν ἱεράν τε καὶ θείαν εἰσελάσαι σκηνήν. Ἀλλ' οὐδ' ἂν προσοίσειε θυσίαν δεκτήν. Γέγραπται γὰρ ἐν τῷ Δευτερονομίῳ· «Οὐκ ἔσται πόρνη ἀπὸ θυγατέρων Ἰσραὴλ, καὶ οὐκ ἔσται πορνεύων ἀπὸ υἱῶν Ἰσραήλ· καὶ οὐκ ἔσται
pass_a_gloss: Continues Cyril's question from §9 ('having brought forward'): [bringing forward] as proof the ending of Solomon's life and what he suffered on the threshold of old age (Homeric phrase). Pall.: How do you mean? Cyr.: He was so bright and famed as to take an incomparable glory, yet he changed over to the unlovely, rather leapt down ignobly to the uttermost of impiety toward God. Quotation 3 Kingdoms 10:23-24 (grew great over all kings in wealth and wisdom, kings sought his face to hear the wisdom the Lord gave in his heart). But pleasure of wicked little women levered him out, as it were removed him from the divine tent and sent him into the pits of idolatry. Quotation 3 Kingdoms 11:1-6 (foreign women nations the Lord forbade, clung, 700 ruling wives, 300 concubines in old age they turned aside,, his heart heart not perfect, Astarte abomination,, of Sidonians 'their king' idol of the sons of Ammon did evil before the Lord). Is it not worth lamenting? He who raised the famous temple, who asked the wisdom that is assessor of the divine thrones (= Wisd 9:4), admired for unequalled understanding to the ends of the earth, conspicuous like the morning star to cities and lands, worsted by shameful women, going after most abominable pleasure, is detected fallen into such folly as to disregard piety toward God. So it is indisputably perilous to be together with foreigners. Utterly dreadful to be worsted by fleshly pleasure; such a one is unclean, hated by the all-pure God, and not without virtue [may one] drive in to the holy and divine tent; nor would he offer an acceptable sacrifice. Written in Deuteronomy: there shall be no prostitute of the daughters of Israel, no fornicator of the sons; and there shall not be [§11 continues].
pass_b_english: Cyril: …the end of Solomon’s life as proof, and what befell him on the very threshold of old age?

Cyril: He was so brilliant and so celebrated that he had, in a sense, already won a glory beyond compare; yet he passed over into what is shameful, or rather he leapt down basely into the very depth of impiety toward God. His story runs like this. It is written in the Third Book of Kingdoms: ‘And Solomon grew greater than all the kings of the earth in wealth and in wisdom. And all the kings of the earth sought the face of Solomon, to hear his wisdom, which the Lord had given in his heart’ (1 Kings 10:23–24). Yet this man, so glorious and so celebrated, who had advanced so far in wisdom that he became an object of boundless wonder even among the most eminent, was pried loose by pleasure in wicked women; and that pleasure, as it were, dragged him out of the divine tent itself and threw him into the pits of idolatry. For it is written of him: ‘And King Solomon was a lover of women, and he took foreign wives, and also the daughter of Pharaoh: Moabite, Ammonite, Edomite, Syrian, Hittite and Amorite women, from the nations about which the Lord had said to the sons of Israel, You shall not go in to them, and they shall not come in to you, lest they turn your hearts aside after their idols. To these Solomon clung in love. And he had seven hundred wives who were princesses, and three hundred concubines. And it came to pass in the time of Solomon’s old age that the foreign wives turned his heart aside after other gods. And his heart was not perfect with the Lord his God, as was the heart of David his father. And Solomon went after Astarte, the abomination of the Sidonians, and after their king, the idol of the sons of Ammon. And Solomon did evil in the sight of the Lord, and did not follow the Lord as David his father did’ (1 Kings 11:1–6).

Is it not right to lament over one who is said to have suffered such things? The man who raised that famous temple in Jerusalem, who asked for the wisdom that sits beside the divine thrones (Wisdom of Solomon 9:4), who was admired for his matchless understanding to the very ends of the earth beneath heaven, who shone like the morning star over cities and lands: overcome by shameful women and following after a most loathsome pleasure, he is found to have fallen into such folly that he utterly disregarded even piety toward God itself. Beyond dispute, then, it is dangerous to keep company with foreigners. And it is altogether terrible to be overcome by fleshly pleasure. Such a man is unclean and hateful to the all-pure God, and without virtue he may not enter the holy and divine tent. Nor could he even offer an acceptable sacrifice. For it is written in Deuteronomy: ‘There shall be no prostitute among the daughters of Israel, and no fornicator among the sons of Israel; and there shall be no… (Deuteronomy 23:17)

anf_compare.notes: No public-domain English of De adoratione Book 14 exists to compare. Translated fresh from the Migne PG 68 Greek on 2026-10-23; the withheld earlier English was not used as a base.

apparatus.note: Migne PG 68 print; the column break may cut a sentence or a word.

Section opens mid-sentence, completing Cyril's question begun at the end of §9 ('…if one brought forward…'); the §9 translator should end on that clause. 'The Third Book of Kingdoms' is the Septuagint title of 1 Kings; LXX 3 Kingdoms 10:23-24 and 11:1-6 match English 1 Kings 10:23-24 and 11:1-6 in numbering. In 11:5 the LXX reads 'their king' (τοῦ βασιλέως αὐτῶν) for Milcom/Molech; kept as 'their king, the idol of the sons of Ammon'. 'The wisdom that sits beside the divine thrones' echoes Wisdom of Solomon 9:4 (τὴν τῶν σῶν θρόνων πάρεδρον σοφίαν), Solomon's prayer, so cited. 'Like the morning star' (ἑωσφόρος) may glance at Isaiah 14:12 (the fallen morning star), but Cyril uses it as praise here; uncited. 'Among the most eminent' renders παρά γε τοῖς ἄγαν διωρισμένοις (could also be 'the most discerning'). 'Without virtue he may not enter the holy and divine tent' renders the elliptical καὶ οὐκ ἀρετῆς δίχα … εἰσελάσαι σκηνήν (an implied 'it is possible'). γύναια is contemptuous ('wretched women'); rendered 'wicked women' with πονηρῶν. The Deuteronomy quotation runs over into §11; citation given at the break. LXX Deuteronomy 23:18 = English 23:17. Reviewer: 'and without virtue he may not enter' keeps ὁ τοιόσδε as the implied subject of the elliptical οὐκ ἀρετῆς δίχα … εἰσελάσαι (earlier draft generalised to 'no one'). ἀπεῖπε in the 1 Kings 11:2 quotation rendered 'had said to' (NETS 'about which the Lord said'); the draft's 'had forbidden the sons of Israel' was ungrammatical.
